question:
I'm swapping out Databricks for DuckDB as my "warehouse" for dbt. Some of my transformations involve creating a Map column in Databricks e.g.:

SELECT
  date,
  col1,
  col2,
  MAP(
      'col1', col1,
      'col2', col2
  ) AS mapped
FROM table1

How would I convert the Map column creation to use DuckDB syntax only?

I've tried these:

{
  'col1': col1,
  'col2': col2
} AS mapped

map{
  'col1': col1,
  'col2': col2
} AS mapped

{
  'col1': col1,
  'col2': col2
}::map(VARCHAR, BIGINT) AS mapped

I know the attempts below create structs and not maps but I wanted to see if I was using the wrong datatype:

struct_pack( col1 := col1, col2 := col2) AS mapped

{
  'col1': col1,
  'col2': col2
}::struct(col1 BIGINT, col2 BIGINT) AS mapped

But none of these seem to work and I get this error:

Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types '+(VARCHAR, BIGINT)'. You might need to add explicit type casts.

Then it lists a bunch of conversions similar to this +(BIGINT) -> BIGINT. The columns value1 and value2 are both integers.

Any ideas how to resolve this or create a Map column in this way? Thanks!
title: Creating a MAP column in DuckDB from existing columns
answer:
Using MAP { ... } works on the following small example:

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE table1 AS
    SELECT 10 AS col1, 123 AS col2 
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 20 AS col1, 456 AS col2;

Running this:

SELECT MAP {'col1': col1, 'col2': col2} AS mapped FROM table1;

Returns the following:

┌───────────────────────┐
│        mapped         │
│ map(varchar, integer) │
├───────────────────────┤
│ {col1=10, col2=123}   │
│ {col1=20, col2=456}   │
└───────────────────────┘
